description:
Extract structural information from a given structure file.

This tool reads a structure file and returns key structural information including 
lattice parameters, chemical formula, number of atoms, cell volume, crystallographic 
density, and molar mass. The amount of detail returned depends on the level parameter.

Args:
    structure_path (Path): Path to the structure file (e.g., CIF, POSCAR, XYZ).
    level: Detail level. 'basic' for lightweight scanning (formula, elements, natoms, lattice_parameters), 
           'standard' for full physical properties (default).

Returns:
    Dict: Dictionary containing:
        - structure_info (Dict): Dictionary with structural information:
            - formula: Chemical formula of the structure
            - formula_dict: Chemical formula as element-count dictionary
            - natoms: Total number of atoms in the structure
            - lattice_parameters: Lattice parameters (a, b, c, alpha, beta, gamma)
            - bond_table_md: Markdown table of bonds (omitted if disordered)
            - angle_table_md: Markdown table of bond angles (omitted if disordered)
            - dihedral_table_md: Markdown table of dihedrals (omitted if disordered)
              Notes: Computed using ASE NeighborList with natural cutoffs ×1.2; includes PBC nearest images;
              caps: bonds≤10k, angles≤50k, dihedrals≤50k. If structure is disordered, geometry is skipped.
            - volume: Unit cell volume in Å³
            - density: Crystallographic density in g/cm³
            - molar_mass: Molar mass in g/mol
            - elements: List of elements present in the structure
        - message (str): Success or error message
name: get_structure_info

description:
Extract molecular information from a given molecule file.

This tool reads a molecule file and returns key molecular information including 
molar mass and chemical formula.

Args:

Returns:

            - formula: Chemical formula of the molecule
            - molar_mass: Molar mass in g/mol
            - bond_table_md: Markdown table of bonds
            - angle_table_md: Markdown table of bond angles
            - dihedral_table_md: Markdown table of dihedrals

description:
Build a bulk crystal structure using ASE.

Args:
    material (str): Element or chemical formula.
    conventional (bool): If True, convert to conventional standard cell.
    crystal_structure (CrystalStructureType | str): Crystal structure type for material1. Must be one of sc, fcc, bcc, hcp, rhombohedral, orthorhombic, mcl, diamond, zincblende, rocksalt, cesiumchloride, fluorite or wurtzite. Default 'fcc'.
    a, b, c, alpha: Lattice parameters.
    output_file (str): Output filename only (e.g. "bulk.cif").

Returns:
    dict with structure_file (Path)
name: build_bulk_structure_by_template

description:
Generates a crystal structure using full crystallographic parameters
and explicit Wyckoff positions.

Parameters
----------
a, b, c : float
    Lattice parameters in Å.
alpha, beta, gamma : float
    Lattice angles in degrees.
spacegroup : str | int
    Space group symbol (e.g. "P42/mnm") or integer number (1–230).
wyckoff_positions : List[WyckoffSite]
    Each entry contains:
        element : str
        coords  : List[float]   (fractional coordinates [x,y,z])
        wyckoff : str
        label   : Optional[str]
output_file : str
    Output filename only (e.g. "structure.cif").

Returns
-------
Dict
    {
        "structure_path": Path | None,
        "code": int,
        "message": str
    }
name: build_bulk_structure_by_wyckoff

description:
Generate a supercell from an existing atomic structure using ASE.

Creates a supercell by repeating the input structure along the three lattice 
directions according to the specified supercell matrix. This is useful for 
creating larger simulation cells or studying periodic boundary effects.

Args:
    structure_path (Path): Path to input structure file. Supports various formats 
        including CIF, POSCAR, XYZ, etc.
    supercell_matrix (list[int]): List of three integers [nx, ny, nz] specifying 
        the number of repetitions along each lattice vector (a, b, c). 
        Default [1, 1, 1] (no supercell expansion).
    output_file (str): Output filename only (e.g. "supercell.cif").

Returns:
    Dict: Dictionary containing:
        - structure_paths (Path): Path to the generated supercell structure file
        - message (str): Success or error message with supercell matrix details
        
Note:
    The supercell will have dimensions (nx × ny × nz) times the original unit cell,
    where nx, ny, nz are the values in supercell_matrix. Total number of atoms
    will be multiplied by (nx × ny × nz).
name: make_supercell_structure

description:
Modify the lattice of a structure using a specified 3x3 matrix.

This tool supports two distinct modes:
1. 'supercell': Creates a supercell by repeating the unit cell. The matrix must represent integer repetitions.
2. 'deformation': Applies an affine transformation (strain/shear) to the lattice vectors.

Args:
    matrix (List[List[float]]): A strict 3x3 matrix. 
        - If mode='supercell': Values will be rounded to integers (e.g., [[2,0,0]...]).
        - If mode='deformation': Values represent the deformation gradient (e.g., [[1.05,0,0]...] for 5% strain).
    mode (Literal["supercell", "deformation"]): The operation mode.
    scale_atoms (bool): Only used in 'deformation' mode. If True, atoms move with the lattice (physical strain).
    output_file (str): Output filename only (e.g. "transformed.cif").
name: apply_structure_transformation

description:
Build a molecule structure from SMILES string using RDKit.

This tool generates a single conformation of a molecule from a SMILES string.
It adds hydrogens and generates 3D coordinates using ETKDGv3, followed by
MMFF force-field optimisation.

Args:
    smiles (str): A valid SMILES string representing the molecule.
    output_file (str): Output filename only. Supported formats: .xyz (default),
        .sdf, .mol, .pdb (e.g. "molecule.xyz").

Returns:
    Dict: Dictionary containing:
        - structure_paths (Path): Path to the generated structure file
        - message (str): Success or error message
name: build_molecule_structures_from_smiles

description:
Add a cell to an existing molecule structure, suitable for ABACUS molecular calculations.

When performing molecular calculations with ABACUS, it is essential to add a sufficiently large cell to the molecule to avoid interactions between periodic images. This tool adds a specified cell to an existing molecule structure, centers the molecule, and allows setting the vacuum thickness.

Args:
    molecule_path (Path): Path to the existing molecule structure file.
    cell (Optional[List[List[float]]]): 3x3 cell vectors in Ångströms. Default is a cubic cell with 10 Å sides.
    vacuum (Optional[float]): Thickness of vacuum layer (Å) added around the molecule. Default is 5.0 Å.
    output_file (str): Output filename only (e.g. "molecule_cell.cif").

Returns:
    Dict: Dictionary containing:
        - structure_paths (Path): Path to the generated structure file
        - message (str): Success or error message

Note:
    For ABACUS molecular calculations, proper cell size and vacuum thickness are crucial to avoid artificial interactions between molecules. It is recommended to set the cell and vacuum large enough for isolated molecule calculations.
name: add_cell_for_molecules

description:
Build a surface slab structure using either molcrys_kit's topological slab generation 
(when repair=True) or ASE's surface builder (when repair=False).

Supports multiple input formats and generates a single surface slab. 

Args:
    material_path (Path):  
        Legacy argument for bulk structure file path.  
    slab_size_mode (Literal["layers", "thickness"]):
        Mode to specify slab size: either "layers" or "thickness".
    slab_size_value (int | float):
        Value for the slab size. If mode is "layers", this should be an integer representing
        the minimum number of atomic layers. If mode is "thickness", this should be a float
        representing the slab thickness in Angstroms.
    miller_index (List[int]):  
        Miller indices (h, k, l). 
    repair (bool):  
        Whether to use molcrys_kit's topological slab generation which preserves molecular
        integrity during slab cutting. If False, uses ASE's surface builder for faster performance. 
        Turn on for covalent-bonded materials, e.g. molecular crystals, organic-inorganic hybrids.
    vacuum (float):  
        The thickness of the vacuum layer in Angstroms (Å). This is always a length unit, 
        independent of slab_size_mode.
    termination (int | float | Callable | str | None):  
        Termination selection strategy (Note: both methods generate a single termination):  
          - `int`: index of the slab in the generated list  
          - `float`: match by slab.shift value  
          - `'auto'` or `None`: automatically select using default heuristic  
          - `Callable`: custom selector `(List[Slab]) -> Slab`  
          Note: When repair=False (ASE) or repair=True (molcrys_kit), only a single termination is generated
    return_all (bool):  
        If True, output filename will have '_0' appended to distinguish from single output (only affects file naming).  
    bonds (List[BondEntry]):  
        Optional bond length list for slab generation. Each entry should contain:
          - elements: Comma-separated element pair like "C,O"
          - distance: Distance value in Angstroms
        Example: [{"elements": "C,O", "distance": 1.4}, {"elements": "O,H", "distance": 0.9}]
        If repair=True and bonds is not provided, default bonds will be generated based on 
        covalent radii of elements in the structure.   
    output_file (str): Output filename only (e.g. "slab.cif").

Returns:
    dict: with keys  
        - `structure_paths` (Path): generated CIF file(s).  
        - `message` (str): status message.  
        - `meta` (dict): metadata including number of terminations and shift values.
name: build_surface_slab

description:
Build a surface-adsorbate structure by placing a molecule onto a surface slab.

Two placement modes are available:
- Legacy mode (default): place the adsorbate at an explicit fractional coordinate
  via the `shift` parameter.
- Pymatgen mode (activated when `site_selector` is provided): use pymatgen
  AdsorbateSiteFinder to automatically locate ontop / bridge / hollow adsorption
  sites, optionally filtered to a specific element (e.g. place water above Ti
  atoms only). This mode overrides `shift` entirely.

In both modes, `orientation` can be used to rotate the adsorbate molecule before
placement, and `anchor_atom_index` controls which atom of the adsorbate is
positioned exactly at the adsorption site coordinate.

Args:
    output_file (str): Output filename only (e.g. "ads.cif").
        When enumerate_all=True used as template: 'ads.cif' → 'ads_site0.cif', 'ads_site1.cif', etc.

    surface_path (Path): Path to the surface slab structure file (CIF, POSCAR, etc.).

    adsorbate_path (Path): Path to the adsorbate molecule structure file.
        The atom ordering in this file determines anchor_atom_index and the
        initial orientation used by the `orientation` parameter.

    shift (Optional[Union[List[float], str]]): [LEGACY MODE ONLY] Position of the
        adsorbate anchor atom on the surface.
        - [x, y]: Fractional coordinates (0.0–1.0) within the surface unit cell.
          Example: [0.5, 0.5] places the adsorbate at the cell center.
        - str: Reserved for future use; ASE named sites are not supported for
          externally-read slabs (raises TypeError if used on a non-ASE-generated slab).
        Ignored when site_selector is provided. Default [0.5, 0.5].

    height (float): Height of the adsorbate anchor atom above the topmost slab
        atom in Ångströms. Applies to both placement modes. Default 2.0.

    site_selector (Optional[AdsorptionSiteSelector]): Activates pymatgen-based
        site finding. When provided, overrides the `shift` parameter entirely.
        When None (default), falls back to legacy `shift`-based placement.
        AdsorptionSiteSelector is a Pydantic model with the following fields:

        - site_type (str): Required. Geometry of the adsorption site. Valid values:
            - 'ontop': directly above a single surface atom.
            - 'bridge': midpoint between two neighboring surface atoms.
            - 'hollow': center of a triangle of surface atoms (Delaunay face center).

        - target_element (Optional[str]): Element symbol (e.g. 'O', 'Ti') to
            restrict candidates to ontop sites above that element only.
            Only valid when site_type='ontop'; raises ValueError otherwise.
            When None (default), all sites of the given site_type are considered.
            Example: target_element='Ti' places the adsorbate above a Ti surface atom.

        - site_index (int): 0-based index into the symmetry-reduced list of
            matching sites returned by pymatgen. Default 0 (first unique site).
            Ignored when enumerate_all=True.
            Tip: set enumerate_all=True first to see how many unique sites exist,
            then call again with the desired site_index.

        Example JSON: {"site_type": "ontop", "target_element": "Ti", "site_index": 0}

    anchor_atom_index (int): Index (0-based) of the atom in the adsorbate file
        that is positioned exactly at the adsorption site coordinate.
        Corresponds to ASE add_adsorbate mol_index. Default 0 (first atom).
        Also serves as the pivot atom when orientation.rotation_center='anchor'.
        Example: for a water file with atom order [O, H, H], anchor_atom_index=0
        places the O atom at the site; anchor_atom_index=1 places the first H.

    orientation (Optional[AdsorbateOrientation]): Rotation applied to the adsorbate
        molecule before placement. When None (default), the molecule is placed
        exactly as it appears in adsorbate_path with no modification.
        AdsorbateOrientation is a Pydantic model with the following fields:

        - rotation (List[float]): Required. Three Euler angles [ax, ay, az] in
            degrees, applied sequentially around the global x, y, z Cartesian axes
            of the slab cell.
            IMPORTANT: the result depends on the initial orientation of the molecule
            in adsorbate_path. There is no automatic normalization or pre-alignment.
            You must know the adsorbate geometry before specifying angles.
            Examples (assuming a water file where O is at the top and both H atoms
            point along the -z direction, i.e. the default O-up orientation):
            - [0, 0, 0] or None: molecule used as-is (O points away from surface)
            - [180, 0, 0]: flip 180° around x-axis → O faces the surface (O-down)
            - [30, 0, 0]: tilt 30° around x-axis
            - [0, 0, 45]: rotate 45° in-plane around z-axis

        - rotation_center (str): Pivot point for the rotation. Default 'COM'.
            - 'COM': rotate around the molecular center of mass. The anchor atom
              may shift slightly during rotation; add_adsorbate then repositions
              anchor_atom_index exactly at the adsorption site.
            - 'anchor': rotate around the anchor_atom_index atom, which stays
              fixed in space. The rest of the molecule pivots around it.
              Use 'anchor' to fix the binding atom while sweeping molecular
              orientation, e.g. keep O fixed above a Ti atom and vary H tilt angle.

        Example JSON: {"rotation": [180, 0, 0], "rotation_center": "COM"}
        Example JSON: {"rotation": [30, 0, 0], "rotation_center": "anchor"}

    enumerate_all (bool): When True, generate one CIF file per symmetry-distinct
        matching site (as identified by site_selector) and return all paths.
        Output filenames are derived from output_file by inserting _siteN before
        the extension: e.g. output_file='ads.cif' → 'ads_site0.cif', 'ads_site1.cif'.
        structure_paths in the return dict will be a List[Path] instead of a single Path.
        Use this to enumerate all inequivalent adsorption configurations.
        Default False (place adsorbate at the single site given by site_selector.site_index).
        Only meaningful when site_selector is provided.

Returns:
    Dict containing:
        - structure_paths (Path or List[Path]): Path(s) to the generated CIF file(s).
          A single Path when enumerate_all=False; a list when enumerate_all=True.
        - code (int): 0 on success, 1 on failure.
        - message (str): Human-readable success summary or error description.

AdsorbateOrientation.description: Controls the rotation applied to an adsorbate molecule before placement on a surface.

rotation.description: Required. [ax, ay, az] Euler angles in degrees around global x, y, z axes.
rotation.title: Rotation

AdsorbateOrientation.title: AdsorbateOrientation

site_index.description: 0-based index into symmetry-reduced site list. Ignored when enumerate_all=True.
site_index.title: Site Index

target_element.description: Element symbol to filter ontop sites, e.g. 'O', 'Ti'. Only valid with site_type='ontop'.
target_element.title: Target Element

Build an interface between two slab structures with lattice matching and strain checking.

description:
Generate crystal structures using CALYPSO with specified chemical species.

CALYPSO is a crystal structure prediction software that generates stable crystal 
configurations through evolutionary algorithms and particle swarm optimization.

Args:
    species (List[str]): List of chemical element symbols (e.g., ['Mg', 'O', 'Si']). 
        These elements will be used as building blocks in structure generation.
        All element symbols must be supported by the internal element property database.
    n_tot (int): Number of CALYPSO structure configurations to generate. Each structure 
        will be created in a separate subdirectory and then collected into the final output.

Returns:
    Dict: Dictionary containing:
        - structure_paths (Path): Directory path containing generated POSCAR files 
          (outputs/poscars_for_optimization/)
        - message (str): Success or error message with generation details
        
Note:
    - Generated structures are saved as POSCAR_0, POSCAR_1, etc. in the output directory
    - Each structure undergoes internal screening and optimization
    - If species or n_tot are not provided, users will be reminded to supply this information
    - Intermediate files are cleaned up, keeping only input.dat and final POSCAR files
name: submit_generate_calypso_structures

description:
Create a defect structure by removing specific molecular clusters based on spatial relationships.

This tool creates vacancy defects in molecular crystals by removing specific molecular units
based on spatial clustering, which is particularly useful for molecular crystals where
entire molecules need to be removed as clusters rather than individual atoms.

Args:
    structure_path (Path): Path to the input molecular crystal structure file (e.g., CIF).
    species_list (Optional[List[DefectSpec]]): List of DefectSpec objects specifying which species to remove and how many. 
        If None, uses the simplest unit in the crystal. Example: [DefectSpec(species_id="C6H14N2_1", count=1), DefectSpec(species_id="H4N_1", count=1)]
    seed_index (Optional[int]): Index of the molecule to start removing from. 
        If None, picks randomly from rarest species.
    method (str): Method to use for selecting molecules to remove. 
        Currently only supports 'spatial_cluster'.
    return_removed_cluster (bool): If True, also returns the cluster of removed molecules as a separate crystal.
    output_file (str): Output filename only (e.g. "defect.cif").
    seed (int): Random seed for reproducibility. Change to get different defect configurations. Default 42.

Returns:
    Dict: Dictionary containing:
        - structure_paths (Path): Path to the generated defective structure file
        - removed_cluster_path (Path): Path to the removed cluster structure file (only when return_removed_cluster is True)
        - message (str): Success or error message

description:
Create a doped structure by substituting elements in a crystal structure.

This tool takes a crystal structure and replaces a fraction of specified elements
with doping elements. It supports simple random replacement as well as advanced
features like Wyckoff site targeting, charge compensation, and supercell expansion.

Basic usage (random replacement):
    doping_elements: [{"original": "Lu", "replacement": "Y", "fraction": 0.2}]

Wyckoff-targeted replacement (replace only at specific crystallographic sites):
    doping_elements: [
        {"original": "Al", "replacement": "Ti", "fraction": 0.25,
         "wyckoff_targets": [{"wyckoff_label": "4a"}]}
    ]

Charge-balanced replacement (auto-compensate when valences differ):
    doping_elements: [
        {"original": "Al", "replacement": "Ti", "fraction": 0.1,
         "oxidation_state_original": 3, "oxidation_state_replacement": 4}
    ]
    charge_compensation: {"enabled": true, "strategy": "auto"}

Args:
    structure_path (Path): Path to the input structure file (e.g., CIF, POSCAR).
    doping_elements (List[dict]): List of substitution specifications. Each dict must contain:
        - original (str): Element symbol to replace, e.g. "Lu"
        - replacement (str): Replacement element or covalent ion name, e.g. "Y" or "methylammonium"
        - fraction (float, optional): Fraction of sites to replace (0-1). Default 1.0.
        - count (int, optional): Exact number of sites to replace (mutually exclusive with fraction).
        - wyckoff_targets (list, optional): Target specific Wyckoff positions,
          e.g. [{"wyckoff_label": "4a"}]. Triggers wyckoff mode automatically.
        - oxidation_state_original (int, optional): Override oxidation state of original element.
        - oxidation_state_replacement (int, optional): Override oxidation state of replacement.
    output_file (str): Output filename only (e.g. "doped.cif").
    seed (int): Random seed for reproducibility. Default 42.
    mode (str, optional): Substitution mode. Default None (auto-detected).
        - "random": Random site selection (default when no wyckoff_targets given)
        - "ordered": Symmetry-preserving replacement by Wyckoff orbit
        - "wyckoff": Replace only at specified Wyckoff positions (auto when wyckoff_targets present)
    supercell (List[int], optional): Supercell dimensions [a, b, c] applied before doping.
        Useful for low-concentration doping, e.g. [2, 2, 2].
    charge_compensation (dict, optional): Charge balance configuration dict.
        Example: {"enabled": true, "strategy": "auto", "anion_species": ["O"]}
        Fields:
        - enabled (bool): Enable charge compensation. Default true.
        - strategy (str): "auto", "anion_adjust", "cation_vacancy", "anion_vacancy", or "mixed".
        - anion_species (list[str], optional): Anion species to adjust, e.g. ["O", "N"].
        - cation_species (list[str], optional): Cation species for vacancy creation.
        - tolerance (float): Charge balance tolerance. Default 0.01.
    validate_structure (bool): Run post-doping validation. Default False.
    min_distance_threshold (float): Minimum allowed interatomic distance in Angstroms. Default 0.5.
    symprec (float): Symmetry precision for spacegroup analysis. Default 0.1.

Returns:
    Dict: Dictionary containing:
        - structure_paths (Path): Path to the generated doped structure file
        - code (int): 0 for success, 1 for failure
        - message (str): Success or error message with doping details
        - validation (dict, optional): Validation results when validate_structure=True

DopingEntry.description:
Flat schema for simple element substitution.

Used by the legacy ``make_doped_structure`` tool.
DopingEntry.title: DopingEntry

description:
Analyze Wyckoff positions in a crystal structure.

This tool identifies all unique Wyckoff sites in the structure, showing which
elements occupy which positions. Useful for planning targeted doping operations.

Args:
    structure_path (Path): Path to the input structure file (e.g., CIF, POSCAR).
    symprec (float): Symmetry precision for space group analysis. Default 0.1.

Returns:

name: analyze_wyckoff_positions

description:
Generate crystal structures using CrystalFormer with specified conditional properties.

This MCP tool requires the agent to ASK THE USER to specify the target space group(s) 
for structure generation. The agent MUST NOT automatically determine or guess space groups - 
the agent should always prompt the user to provide the space group number(s).

Args:
    cond_model_type_list (List[str]): List of conditional model types. Supported types:
        'bandgap', 'shear_modulus', 'bulk_modulus', 'ambient_pressure', 'high_pressure', 'sound'.
        'bandgap' returns the bandgap value in eV,
        'shear_modulus' returns the shear modulus in log10 GPa,
        'bulk_modulus' returns the bulk modulus in log10 GPa,
        'ambient_pressure' returns the superconducting critical temperature at ambient pressure in K,
        'high_pressure' returns the superconducting critical temperature at high pressure in K,
        'sound' returns the sound velocity in m/s.
        Note: All model types must be supported by the CrystalFormer model.
        - When multiple properties are provided, they will be optimized together in a multi-objective manner.
        - When only one property is provided, it will be optimized as a single objective.
        - The agent should ensure that the provided model types are valid and supported by CrystalFormer.
    target_value_list (List[float]): Target values for each property in cond_model_type_list.
    target_type_list (List[str]): Type of target optimization for each property. Options:
        'equal', 'greater', 'less', 'minimize'. Note: for 'minimize', use small target values
        to avoid division by zero.
    space_group (int): **MUST BE PROVIDED BY USER** - Space group number (1-230) that the 
        agent should obtain by asking the user. The agent should never guess or automatically 
        select this value.
        - When random_spacegroup_num=0: Only this user-specified space group will be used
        - When random_spacegroup_num>0: This serves as the minimum space group number
    sample_num (int): Total initial number of samples to generate. When random_spacegroup_num=0,
        all samples use the specified space group. When random_spacegroup_num>0, this total is
        divided equally among the randomly selected space groups.
    random_spacegroup_num (int): Number of random space groups to sample. Default 0.
        - If 0: Generate structures only using the user-specified space_group
        - If >0: Randomly sample this many space groups from the range [space_group, 230]
          where space_group is the user-provided minimum value
    mc_steps (int): Number of Monte Carlo steps for structure optimization. Default 500.

Returns:
    Dict: Dictionary containing:
        - structure_paths (Path): Directory path containing generated structure files
        - message (str): Success or error message

Critical Agent Instructions:
    - ALWAYS ask the user to specify the space group number before using this tool
    - DO NOT make assumptions about which space group to use
    - DO NOT automatically select a space group based on other parameters
    - The user must explicitly provide the space_group parameter value
    - If the user doesn't know which space group to use, help them understand the options (1-230)
    - All input lists (cond_model_type_list, target_value_list, target_type_list) must have 
      the same length for consistency in multi-objective optimization.
    - Alpha weighting values are automatically set to 1.0 for most targets and 0.01 for 'minimize' targets.
name: submit_generate_crystalformer_structures

description:
Pack molecules into a periodic box to generate an amorphous (disordered) structure.

Uses PACKMOL as the packing engine, which optimises molecular placement to avoid
atomic overlaps while filling the box to the requested density.  Accepts molecules
in any format readable by ASE (XYZ, SDF, CIF, …), including polymer chain SDF files
produced by build_polymer_chain.

Three operating modes — provide exactly two of the three size/count parameters:

Mode 1 (box_size + density):   calculates the number of molecules.
Mode 2 (box_size + molecule_numbers): calculates the resulting density.
Mode 3 (density + molecule_numbers): calculates the required cubic box side.

Args:
    molecule_paths (List[Path]): Paths to the molecule files to pack.
    molecule_numbers (Optional[Union[int, List[int]]]): Number of copies of each
        molecule type.  A single integer applies to all types equally.
    box_size (Optional[List[float]]): Box dimensions [a, b, c] in Ångströms.
    density (Optional[float]): Target density in g/cm³.
    composition (Optional[List[float]]): Mole fractions for each molecule type
        (used only with Mode 1).  Equal fractions assumed when not provided.
    output_file (str): Output filename only (e.g. "amorphous.cif").
    seed (int): Random seed passed to PACKMOL.  Default 42.

Returns:
    Dict:
        - structure_paths (Path): Path to the generated CIF file.
        - message (str): Summary including atom count, box, and density.
name: make_amorphous_structure

description:
Form covalent crosslinks between reactive atoms in an amorphous structure using
a purely geometric (heuristic) algorithm — no MD or energy minimisation.

The tool identifies atoms of the specified element types, finds all pairs within
cutoff_distance, and greedily assigns bonds until target_conversion is reached
while respecting max_bonds_per_atom.  Atomic positions are NOT moved; the output
is the same structure annotated with a separate bond-topology JSON file.

Typical workflow:
    1. build_polymer_chain  →  SDF files for each chain type
    2. make_amorphous_structure  →  packed CIF (many chains in a box)
    3. make_crosslinked_structure  →  crosslinked CIF + bonds JSON

Args:
    structure_path (Path): Path to the input structure file (CIF, XYZ, …).
    reactive_specs (List[ReactiveSpec]): One or more element-pair specifications,
        each a dict with keys "element1" and "element2" (element symbols, e.g.
        {"element1": "N", "element2": "C"}).  Setting element1 == element2
        enables self-crosslinking (e.g. radical polymerisation).
    output_file (str): Output filename only (e.g. "crosslinked.cif").
    bonds_output_file (str): Output filename only for bond-topology JSON. Default "crosslink_bonds.json".
    cutoff_distance (float): Maximum distance in Å between two reactive atoms for
        a crosslink to be considered.  Default 4.0 Å.
    target_conversion (float): Fraction of the smaller reactive-atom pool to
        crosslink (0–1).  Default 0.8.
    max_bonds_per_atom (int): Maximum new crosslink bonds per reactive atom.
        Default 1.
    seed (int): Random seed for reproducibility.  Default 42.

Returns:
    Dict:
        - structure_path (Path): Path to the output structure file.
        - bonds_path (Path): Path to the bond-topology JSON file.
        - n_crosslinks (int): Number of crosslink bonds formed.
        - actual_conversion (float): Fraction of reactive sites that were crosslinked.
        - message (str): Summary message.

Note:
    - Positions are heuristic starting points; run energy minimisation or MD
      equilibration before production simulations.
    - The bonds JSON can be loaded by downstream tools to assemble full topology
      (e.g. for GROMACS or other MD packages).
name: make_crosslinked_structure

description:
Add hydrogen atoms in a molecular crystal based on geometric rules.

This tool adds hydrogen atoms to a molecular crystal structure based on 
specified geometric and coordination rules. It can be used to complete the 
structure of molecules by adding hydrogens according to their bonding patterns.

Args:
    - structure_path (Path): Path to the input structure file (e.g., CIF, POSCAR, XYZ).
    - output_file (str): Output filename only (e.g. "hydrogenated.cif").
    - target_elements (Optional[List[str]]): List of atomic symbols to specifically hydrogenate. 
        Only these elements will have hydrogens added. If None or empty, no elements will be targeted.
    - optimize_torsion (bool): Whether to perform conformational optimization to adjust 
        torsion angles. Default is False to preserve ring structures and crystal packing.
    - rules (Optional[List[HydrogenPlacementRule]]): List of rules for coordination geometry. 
        Each rule specifies how hydrogen atoms should be placed around certain atoms.
        Format:
        [
            {
                "symbol": str,              # Required. E.g., "O", "N"
                "neighbors": List[str],     # Optional. E.g., ["Cl", "S"]. Context condition.
                "target_coordination": int, # Optional. Override coordination.
                "geometry": str             # Optional. Override geometry.
            },
            ...
        ]
        
        Processing Logic:
        1. Specific rules (with neighbors) take priority
        2. General rules (without neighbors) take second priority
        3. Default rules are used if no user rules match
    - bond_lengths (Optional[List[BondLengthRule]]): List of bond length rules for specific atom pairs.
        Each rule specifies the bond length between two atoms.
        Format:
        [
            {
                "atom1": str,           # Required. First atom symbol, e.g., "H"
                "atom2": str,           # Required. Second atom symbol, e.g., "O" 
                "length": float         # Required. Bond length in Angstroms
            },
            ...
        ]
        Or can be None to use default bond lengths.

Returns:
    Dict: Dictionary containing:
        - structure_paths (Path): Path to the generated hydrogenated structure file
        - message (str): Success or error message

description:
Build a single isolated polymer chain and return its 3-D structure as an SDF file.

IMPORTANT — OUTPUT SCOPE: This tool produces ONE isolated polymer chain in SDF
format. The output has NO simulation box, NO periodic boundary conditions, and NO
molecular packing. It is NOT a ready-to-use input for MD or DFT simulations. If
you need a simulation-ready system (e.g. for GROMACS or LAMMPS), pass the
output SDF to the make_amorphous_structure tool as a subsequent step.

Use this tool whenever a user asks to "generate", "create", "build", or "construct"
a polymer, copolymer, star polymer, branched polymer, dendrimer, graft copolymer,
cyclic polymer, or any similar macromolecular chain topology.

Args:
    monomers (List[MonomerSpec]): One or more monomer specifications. Each entry
        must have exactly one of:
          - monomer_name (str): A name or alias from the built-in MONOMER_LIBRARY
            (case-insensitive). See the Monomer Library section below.
          - smiles (str): A SMILES string with exactly two [*] wildcard atoms
            marking the head and tail connection points (e.g. "[*]CC[*]").
        Each entry also accepts:
          - repeat_number (int, required, >= 1): Units in this segment/arm/block.
          - ratio (float, optional, 0–1): Mole fraction for random copolymers.
          - configuration_flip_ratio (float, default 0.0): Tacticity control.
          - head_to_tail_flip_ratio (float, default 0.0): Regioregularity control.
          - charge (int, default 0): Formal charge per repeat unit.

    architecture (str, default "linear"): The overall chain topology.

        Architecture Types:
          - "linear"       : A single unbranched chain. Supports all polymer_method
                             options. Required for homopolymers, block, random,
                             alternating, and gradient copolymers.
                             Examples: polyethylene, PS-b-PB, EVA random copolymer.
          - "star"         : Multiple identical arms radiating from a central atom.
                             Requires num_arms. Use 1 monomer in monomers[].
                             Examples: 4-arm star PEG, 6-arm star PMMA.
          - "branched"     : A backbone with pendant side chains.
                             Requires num_branches and branch_length.
                             monomers[0] = backbone monomer,
                             monomers[1] = branch monomer (optional; defaults to
                             same as backbone for simple branched homopolymers).
                             Examples: branched PE, branched PVA.
          - "cyclic"       : A ring polymer (no chain ends). Use 1 monomer.
                             Requires repeat_number >= 3.
                             Examples: cyclic PEG, cyclic PDMS.
          - "graft"        : Backbone + chemically distinct side chains.
                             Requires 2 monomers: monomers[0]=backbone,
                             monomers[1]=sidechain. Requires num_branches
                             (graft density) and branch_length (graft length).
                             Examples: PE-g-PS, PB-g-PAA.
          - "hyperbranched": Irregular dendritic structure with random branching.
                             Use 1 monomer. Total units = sum of repeat_numbers.
                             Examples: hyperbranched polyester, hyperbranched polyether.
          - "dendrimer"    : Perfectly symmetric radial tree structure.
                             Requires generation (number of branching shells).
                             Use 1 monomer. monomers[0].repeat_number = core length.
                             Examples: PAMAM G3, polylysine G2.

    polymer_method (str, default "homopolymer"): Monomer sequence arrangement.
        Only relevant for architecture="linear" with 2+ monomers.

        Polymer Method Types:
          - "homopolymer"  : Single monomer repeated N times (use 1 monomer).
                             Equivalent to polymer_method="".
          - "block"        : Blocks in order: A×n then B×m then C×p...
                             Use >=2 monomers with repeat_number per block.
                             Example: PS(25)-b-PB(20) → 2 monomers, repeat 25 and 20.
          - "random"       : Monomers randomly shuffled. Use >=2 monomers.
                             Set repeat_number proportional to desired composition,
                             or set ratio directly.
                             Example: 60% styrene, 40% acrylate → ratio 0.6 / 0.4.
          - "alternating"  : Strict A-B-A-B... repeating pattern. Use >=2 monomers
                             with equal repeat_numbers (or the pattern cycles
                             through all monomers round-robin).
          - "gradient"     : Composition transitions linearly from monomer A to
                             monomer B along the chain. Use exactly 2 monomers.
                             repeat_number sets total units per monomer segment.

    num_arms (int, optional): Number of arms for architecture="star". Must be >= 2.
        Examples: 4 for a 4-arm star, 6 for a 6-arm star.
        Only used when architecture="star". Ignored otherwise.

    num_branches (int, optional): Number of branch attachment points for
        architecture="branched" or "graft". Branches are placed at evenly spaced
        intervals along the backbone.
        Examples: 2 for 2-branch polymer, 5 for 5-graft copolymer.
        Ignored for other architectures.

    branch_length (int, optional): Number of repeat units per branch or graft
        side chain. For architecture="branched" or "graft".
        If omitted, defaults to repeat_number of the branch monomer.
        Ignored for other architectures.

    generation (int, optional): Number of branching generations for
        architecture="dendrimer". generation=0 → core only; generation=1 → first
        shell; generation=3 → classic G3 dendrimer.
        Required when architecture="dendrimer". Ignored otherwise.

    branching_factor (int, default 2): Number of sub-branches per terminal node
        per generation in dendrimers (architecture="dendrimer") and
        hyperbranched polymers (architecture="hyperbranched").
        Classic PAMAM uses branching_factor=2.

    head_group (str, default "H"): Element symbol for the atom capping the chain
        head terminus. Use "H" for hydrogen termination (most common).
        Ignored for cyclic polymers (no chain ends).

    tail_group (str, default "H"): Element symbol for the atom capping the chain
        tail terminus. Use "H" for hydrogen termination.
        Ignored for cyclic polymers.

    torsion_angle (float, default 90.0): Dihedral angle (degrees) applied
        between consecutive monomers during chain assembly. Controls the
        global chain conformation. 90° gives a helical backbone; 180° gives
        a more extended all-trans conformation.

    use_clean (bool, default False): If True, apply MMFF94/UFF force-field
        geometry optimisation after chain assembly. Improves bond lengths and
        angles but is slower and may fail on unusual topologies. Recommended
        for cyclic polymers to relax ring strain.

    output_file (str, default "polymer_chain.sdf"): Output filename only (e.g. "polymer_chain.sdf").

Returns:
    Dict containing:
      - structure_paths (Path): Path to the generated SDF file.
      - code (int): 0 on success, 1 on failure.
      - message (str): Status description. On success, includes a reminder
        that the output is a single chain requiring further processing for
        simulation use.

Monomer Library (built-in monomer_name values and aliases):
    The following monomer names and aliases are recognised
    (all case-insensitive):

    Vinyl / addition polymers:
      ethylene       → aliases: polyethylene, pe, 乙烯, 聚乙烯
      propylene      → aliases: polypropylene, pp, 丙烯, 聚丙烯
      styrene        → aliases: polystyrene, ps, 苯乙烯, 聚苯乙烯
      vinyl_chloride → aliases: pvc, 氯乙烯, 聚氯乙烯
      vinyl_alcohol  → aliases: pva, pvoh, 乙烯醇, 聚乙烯醇
      vinyl_acetate  → aliases: pvac, 醋酸乙烯酯, 聚醋酸乙烯酯
      acrylonitrile  → aliases: pan, 丙烯腈, 聚丙烯腈
      acrylic_acid   → aliases: paa, 丙烯酸, 聚丙烯酸
      methyl_methacrylate → aliases: mma, pmma, 甲基丙烯酸甲酯, 聚甲基丙烯酸甲酯
      tetrafluoroethylene → aliases: ptfe, 四氟乙烯, 聚四氟乙烯

    Diene polymers:
      butadiene      → aliases: polybutadiene, pb, 丁二烯, 聚丁二烯
      isoprene       → aliases: polyisoprene, pi, 异戊二烯, 聚异戊二烯

    Condensation / heterochain:
      ethylene_oxide → aliases: peg, peo, 环氧乙烷, 聚乙二醇, 聚环氧乙烷
      lactic_acid    → aliases: pla, 乳酸, 聚乳酸
      caprolactone   → aliases: pcl, 己内酯, 聚己内酯
      carbonate      → aliases: pc, polycarbonate, 碳酸酯, 聚碳酸酯
      amide          → aliases: nylon, polyamide, pa, 酰胺, 聚酰胺
      dimethylsiloxane → aliases: pdms, siloxane, 二甲基硅氧烷, 聚二甲基硅氧烷

    Specialty / functional:
      maleic_anhydride → aliases: pma, 马来酸酐
      aniline          → aliases: polyaniline, pani, 苯胺, 聚苯胺, 翡翠绿
      pyrrole          → aliases: polypyrrole, ppy, 吡咯, 聚吡咯
      lysine           → aliases: polylysine, 赖氨酸, 聚赖氨酸
      amidoamine       → aliases: pamam, 酰胺胺, 聚酰胺胺
      ester            → aliases: polyester, pet, 酯, 聚酯
      ether            → aliases: polyether, 醚, 聚醚
      carbon_monoxide  → aliases: 一氧化碳

Examples:
    # Prompt 1: "生成一个含有50个重复单元的线性聚乙烯链"
    build_polymer_chain(
        monomers=[{"monomer_name": "聚乙烯", "repeat_number": 50}],
        architecture="linear",
        polymer_method="homopolymer",
        output_file="polyethylene_50.sdf"
    )

    # Prompt 7: "构造聚苯乙烯和聚丁二烯的嵌段共聚物，每段25个单体"
    build_polymer_chain(
        monomers=[
            {"monomer_name": "styrene", "repeat_number": 25},
            {"monomer_name": "butadiene", "repeat_number": 25},
        ],
        architecture="linear",
        polymer_method="block",
        output_file="PS_b_PB.sdf"
    )

    # Prompt 5: "产生一个四臂星形聚合物，每臂为15个单元的聚氯乙烯链"
    build_polymer_chain(
        monomers=[{"monomer_name": "pvc", "repeat_number": 15}],
        architecture="star",
        num_arms=4,
        output_file="star_PVC_4arm.sdf"
    )

    # Prompt 6: "生成一个含有25个环氧乙烷单元的环状聚乙二醇分子"
    build_polymer_chain(
        monomers=[{"monomer_name": "peg", "repeat_number": 25}],
        architecture="cyclic",
        use_clean=True,
        output_file="cyclic_PEG_25.sdf"
    )

    # Prompt 36: "生成聚乙烯主链上接枝聚苯乙烯侧链的接枝共聚物，主链50个单元，5个侧链各10个单元"
    build_polymer_chain(
        monomers=[
            {"monomer_name": "ethylene", "repeat_number": 50},
            {"monomer_name": "styrene", "repeat_number": 10},
        ],
        architecture="graft",
        num_branches=5,
        branch_length=10,
        output_file="PE_g_PS.sdf"
    )

    # Prompt 21: "生成乙烯和丙烯的无规共聚物，总共40个单体，比例1:1"
    build_polymer_chain(
        monomers=[
            {"monomer_name": "ethylene", "repeat_number": 20},
            {"monomer_name": "propylene", "repeat_number": 20},
        ],
        architecture="linear",
        polymer_method="random",
        output_file="EP_random_copolymer.sdf"
    )

Notes:
    - SMILES connection points: When providing a custom SMILES via the
      smiles field, use exactly two [*] atoms to mark the head and tail
      connection sites. Example: "[*]CC([*])C" for polypropylene.
      The [*] atoms will be replaced by H atoms used as placeholders
      to identify connection geometry.

    - Cross-parameter constraints:
        * num_arms is ONLY used when architecture="star"
        * num_branches and branch_length are ONLY used for "branched" / "graft"
        * generation and branching_factor are ONLY used for "dendrimer" /
          "hyperbranched"
        * polymer_method is ONLY relevant for architecture="linear"

    - Output is a single chain: The SDF file contains one isolated polymer
      molecule with no simulation box and no periodic boundary conditions.
      It is NOT suitable as a direct input for MD or DFT calculations.
      To build a simulation-ready system, pass the output SDF to the
      make_amorphous_structure tool.

    - Geometry quality: With use_clean=False (default), bond lengths may
      be approximate. Set use_clean=True for better geometry at the cost
      of longer computation time. Always set use_clean=True for cyclic
      polymers to avoid unrealistic ring strain.

MonomerSpec.description:
Specification of a single monomer repeat unit for polymer chain building.

Exactly one of ``monomer_name`` or ``smiles`` must be provided. When
``monomer_name`` is given, the SMILES is looked up from the built-in
``MONOMER_LIBRARY`` which includes 20+ common polymer monomers with both
English and Chinese aliases.  When ``smiles`` is given, the caller must
mark exactly two atoms as connection points using the ``[*]`` wildcard
atom notation (standard polymer SMILES convention).

Fields
------
monomer_name : str, optional
    Case-insensitive name or alias from the built-in monomer library.
    Examples: ``"ethylene"``, ``"聚乙烯"``, ``"PS"``, ``"PMMA"``.
    See the ``MONOMER_LIBRARY`` dict for the full list.  Either this or
    ``smiles`` must be set; providing both raises a validation error.
smiles : str, optional
    A SMILES string with exactly two ``[*]`` atoms marking the head and
    tail connection points of the repeat unit.  Example: ``"[*]CC[*]"``
    for polyethylene.  Either this or ``monomer_name`` must be set.
repeat_number : int
    Number of times this monomer is repeated in the chain (or in its
    block/arm segment).  Must be >= 1.  Required.
ratio : float, optional
    Mole fraction of this monomer relative to all monomers in the
    mixture.  Only relevant when ``polymer_method="random"`` is used at
    the top level.  Values must be in [0, 1].  If omitted for random
    copolymers, each monomer's fraction is derived from its
    ``repeat_number`` relative to the total.
configuration_flip_ratio : float
    Fraction of this monomer's occurrences that will be mirror-reflected
    along the head-tail axis (controls tacticity / stereo-chemistry).
    Range [0, 1], default 0.0 (all same configuration = isotactic).
head_to_tail_flip_ratio : float
    Fraction of this monomer's occurrences whose head/tail orientation
    will be reversed (controls regioregularity).  Range [0, 1], default
    0.0 (all head-to-tail = regioregular).
charge : int
    Formal charge of one repeat unit.  Used only when topology files are
    generated downstream.  Default 0.

description:
Extract individual molecules from a molecular crystal and save each to a separate file.

Uses MolCrysKit to identify molecules within the crystal via graph-based bonding,
then writes each molecule to the specified output directory. Optionally unwraps
molecules that span periodic boundaries so they are exported as contiguous geometries.

Args:
    crystal_path (Path): Path to the input crystal file (CIF or other ASE-readable
        periodic structure).
    output_format (Literal["xyz", "cif", "sdf"]): Output format for each molecule file.
        Default "xyz".
    output_dir (str): Directory name to store extracted molecule files. Created if absent.
        Default "extracted_molecules".
    unwrap (bool): If True, use unwrapped molecules (recommended for molecules that
        cross cell boundaries). Default True.
    bond_thresholds (Optional[Dict[str, float]]): Optional bonding cutoffs, e.g.
        {"C-N": 1.6, "O-H": 1.2}. Keys are "Elem1-Elem2"; values are max bond length in Å.

Returns:
    Dict: Contains structure_paths (output directory), molecule_files (list of paths),
    num_molecules, unique_formulas (formula -> count), and message.
name: extract_molecules_from_crystal
